faqs.q: How much does it cost to hire a game development studio?
faqs.guidance: Explain the cost drivers (scope, platforms, art, multiplayer) and that we quote per project after a call; no invented ranges.

faqs.q: What is the difference between co-development and outsourcing?
faqs.guidance: Co-development means our developers work inside your repo, tools, and schedule; outsourcing hands off a defined piece. Say which the studio offers (owner to confirm).

faqs.q: Can you build an online multiplayer game?
faqs.guidance: Yes: Sheep Tag 2 supports up to 32 players online on Photon Quantum with prediction and rollback, US, EU, and AU servers, and bots.

faqs.q: Can you help release our game on Steam?
faqs.guidance: Yes: we released Hypno Halo on Steam and handled Steam integration, achievements, Steam Cloud, and release QA for The Brave Hearts II as its publisher.

faqs.q: Can you port our game to Nintendo Switch?
faqs.guidance: We have released our own games (Hypno Halo, ParaLily) on Nintendo Switch; say porting a client game is case by case and needs the client's platform access; add the Nintendo trademark note.

faqs.q: Which engines do you use?
faqs.guidance: Unity and C# first; Jeremy also works in Unreal Engine 5 and C++ (about-jeremy). Do not claim Godot or others.

faqs.q: Who owns the code and the game when the project ends?
faqs.guidance: Owner decision; state the studio's actual contract position or leave this question out.

pages.notes: Head term 'game development company' is dominated by large outsourcers; the page wins on long-tail: 'indie game co-development studio', 'Unity multiplayer game developer', 'Steam release help'. Label client titles (Cell to Singularity, Citytopia, Travelers Refrain, Lanebreak) as games we contributed to; they are not ours. 'What clients say' uses the Freelancer.com review by Sqe187, quoted exactly with a link to freelancer.com/u/LunaWolfStudios.html. The review does not name a project, so do not attach it to one.

faqs.q: What is a custom Unity editor tool?
faqs.guidance: Code that runs inside the Unity Editor (windows, inspectors, menu items, importers) so a team does repeated work faster; it does not ship in the game build, as Scriptable Sheets' listing notes for itself.

faqs.q: What kinds of editor tools can you build?
faqs.guidance: Name archive-backed examples: a spreadsheet data editor (Scriptable Sheets), an asset import pipeline with scene generation and diagnostics (Jeremy's PS1 asset importer R&D), and an in-editor bug reporter (Jeff's Trello tutorial video).

faqs.q: Can you build tools for designers who don't code?
faqs.guidance: Yes; Scriptable Sheets lets anyone edit game data in a table, with copy and paste from Google Sheets and other flat files (Asset Store listing and forum thread).

faqs.q: Can you extend or fix a tool our team already built?
faqs.guidance: Owner decision; if yes, say we start by reading the existing code and agreeing what to keep.

faqs.q: Will the tool work with our Unity version?
faqs.guidance: We build for the version the client uses; cite only versions the team confirms, and Scriptable Sheets' supported versions from its live listing.

faqs.q: What do we get at handover?
faqs.guidance: Describe what the studio delivers (source, docs, a walkthrough); Scriptable Sheets ships with documentation on GitHub and a video walkthrough as the model. Owner confirms.

faqs.q: Who owns the source code of a custom tool?
faqs.guidance: Owner decision; state the studio's contract position or leave this question out.

pages.notes: Owns 'custom Unity editor tools', 'Unity editor extensions', and 'pipeline and workflow tooling' (tools that run inside the editor). Build servers and CI/CD stay on /services/unity-development/; link there for them. The SERP for these is Fiverr gigs and Unity docs, with no studio pages. Proof order: Scriptable Sheets (Asset Store; say 'recognized at the 17th Unity Awards' until the official term is verified), the four archived Asset Store reviews quoted exactly (Quevanto, Katerlad, deleo, RestingOwl) with the link to the listing's reviews, Jeff's Kodeco ScriptableObject tutorial, and the PS1 importer R&D (a research project, not a product). Do not add Review markup for Asset Store reviews (Google does not allow reviews copied from other sites). 1,000 to 1,500 words.
